hints: Look closely at the three numbers: -198, -212 and -224 kPa. Which one is the least negative (closest to zero) and which one is the most negative?
Remember water always moves down its water potential gradient, from the higher (less negative) value to the lower (more negative) value. Try ranking P, Q and R first.
walkthrough:
**Recall the golden rule for water movement**

Think of water potential like a downhill slope. Water always flows downhill, from higher water potential to lower water potential.

With negative numbers, higher means less negative (closer to zero):
$$higher \; \Psi \rightarrow lower \; \Psi$$

**Rank the three cells**

Let us put P, Q and R in order. P is $-198\,kPa$, R is $-212\,kPa$, Q is $-224\,kPa$.

So from highest to lowest: P (-198) > R (-212) > Q (-224). P has the most water to give, Q has the strongest pull.

**Work out each net movement**

P to R: $-198$ to $-212$ is downhill, so P → R. P to Q: $-198$ to $-224$ is downhill, so P → Q. R to Q: $-212$ to $-224$ is downhill, so R → Q.

All three flows point toward Q, the lowest water potential. That matches option A.

options.A: Correct. P is highest so loses water to both R and Q, and R is higher than Q so loses water to Q. All movements are high to low.
options.B: Almost right but incomplete. It correctly shows P → Q and P → R but misses that R (-212) is also higher than Q (-224), so R → Q must also occur.
options.C: Incorrect direction. This shows water moving from low to high (Q to P and R), which is uphill and opposite to osmosis.
options.D: Incorrect direction. Q (-224) is the lowest water potential so it gains water, it cannot be the source for flow into P.
